questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates familiarity with modern CI/CD threat models and practical security controls beyond basic IAM configuration. Candidates should demonstrate understanding of the software supply chain attack surface and compensating controls.

## Key Concepts
- CI/CD secret scanning: Automated detection of hardcoded credentials in code and configuration
- SBOM generation: Structured inventory of software components for vulnerability tracking
- Code signing: Cryptographic verification of artifact authenticity and integrity
- Dependency pinning: Locking versions to prevent supply chain attacks from transitive dependencies
- Container scanning: Automated analysis of container images for known vulnerabilities
- Ephemeral runners: Short-lived build environments that reduce persistent compromise risk

## Success Criteria
- Secret scanning blocks all committed secrets before merge
- All dependencies pinned with < 5% known vulnerabilities in production
- SBOMs generated for 100% of released artifacts
- Container scans run on every image build with zero high-severity CVEs in production
- Incident response playbook tested quarterly with < 24-hour detection-to-resolution time

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question probes advanced defense-in-depth for supply-chain risk, blending build-time SBOM governance with runtime attestation and automated policy enforcement. It also evaluates the candidate's understanding of multi-tenant security isolation and incident response workflows that minimize blast radius.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime attestation: Verifying container integrity before execution
- SBOM (Software Bill of Materials): Inventory of software components for vulnerability tracking
- Sigstore cosign: Open-source image signing and verification tool
- OPA Gatekeeper / Kyverno: Kubernetes admission controllers for policy enforcement
- CI SBOM integration: Automated artifact scanning during the build phase
- Per-tenant isolation: Namespace-level security boundaries in multi-tenant clusters
- Incident response playbooks: Structured procedures for rapid threat response

## Code Example
```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
  image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
  not verified_image[image]
  msg := sprintf("Image '%v' is not signed or lacks a valid SBOM", [image])
}

verified_image[image] {
  cosign.verify(image)
  sbom_exists(image)
}

sbom_exists(image) {
  input.review.object.metadata.annotations["sbom.id"]
}
```

## Success Criteria
1. All production images are signed with cosign before registry admission
2. SBOM覆盖率 reaches 100% for critical workloads
3. Gatekeeper/Kyverno policies block 100% of unsigned images at admission time
4. Tenant namespaces are isolated with zero cross-tenant network access
5. IR playbook execution achieves containment within 1 hour of alert

## Why This Is Asked

```rego
deny[msg] {

}
```
